If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (alternating 0.33/1.00) in the last 5 days, apply a 3–7% downward correction to forecast at 15–25 day horizon to dampen volatility overreaction.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for late horizon (26–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, add 3–5% to forecast at 10–15 day horizon to counteract sentiment-overlooked upside.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is trending upward, subtract 3–5% from forecast at 10–15 day horizon to align with sentiment-driven downside expectation.
